slides.title: Design, Packaging, and Sustainability
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 8 English, Unit 2: Design, Packaging, and Sustainability. At its centre is "Signal in the Static", an investigative story in which two student journalists, Imani and Kofi, follow an anonymous tip about a secret land deal that threatens their city's community gardens. Around the story you will study how design and packaging shape the messages we trust, and why sustainable communication matters as much as sustainable materials. You will master 30 vocabulary words about investigation, emotion and public life, make partitive expressions your primary grammar focus, and practise zero and first conditionals, relative clauses, comparatives and superlatives, formal questions beginning with prepositions, and the passive voice. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to read and analyse a narrative text, identifying themes of truth, bias, manipulation, and civic responsibility. You will also use partitive expressions correctly and confidently in both speaking and writing (e.g., a piece of evidence, a surge of indignation, a multitude of voices). You will also form and use zero and first conditionals to express general truths and real future possibilities. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: exult, loathe, usurp, feign, intervene, obstruct. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: Packaging the Truth: How Design Shapes What We Believe
On Air, On Record: An Interview with Producer Amara
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Packaging the Truth: How Design Shapes What We Believe and On Air, On Record: An Interview with Producer Amara. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: Partitive Expressions

slides.narration: The first language focus is Partitive Expressions. Partitive expressions name a portion of something, so instead of vague sentences like "I want cake" or "She felt happiness" you can say "I want a piece of cake" or "She felt a surge of happiness." They matter most with uncountable nouns such as water, information and excitement, which cannot take a number on their own. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Vocabulary Expert Interview. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
